summary: A toggle for an on/off setting that takes effect as soon as it is flipped. It is a form control: it submits a value while on, resets with its form, is disabled by a disabled fieldset and validates required. It has a label, a description, an error message and two sizes.

label.note: The visible text and the accessible name. Empty is a defect: a console warning names it.

description.note: A hint under the label, read with the control.

errorMessage.note: Why the setting is not accepted. Shown, and read with the control, only while validation is error.

selected.note: On. The form-reset state is the initial value of this prop. The native name checked is an alias in the API vocabulary and is not used.

validation.note: error shows the error look and the error message and marks the control invalid for assistive technology. Set by the author; it does not follow the required check by itself.

disabled.note: Cannot be focused or toggled, and its value is not submitted. A disabled ancestor fieldset has the same effect without changing this prop.

required.note: The switch must be on for the form to be valid.

name.note: The name the value is submitted under.

value.note: What is submitted under name while the switch is on. Nothing is submitted while it is off.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.notes: The host: label row and the messages in one column.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: The native input that carries the switch role, focus and validity.

anatomy.name: track
anatomy.notes: The pill that shows on or off.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: The knob that sits at the start when off and the end when on.

anatomy.name: content
anatomy.notes: Column beside the control holding label, description and error message.

anatomy.name: errorMessage
anatomy.notes: Shown when validation is error and errorMessage is set.

label.notes: Carried by the label prop, not a slot.

change.note: Fired after the person flips the switch, once selected and the form value are updated. Not fired for a change made through the prop or by form reset.

disabled.trigger: disabled is true or a disabled fieldset contains it.
disabled.note: Dimmed, no pointer or keyboard operation.

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop. A <label for> activates the control but does not name it.

formAssociation.note: Submits value under name while selected; null while off. Form reset restores the initial selected. A disabled fieldset disables it. required is valid only while on. Group-less: no radio-style exclusivity.

accessibility.targetSize: The pointer target, including the label, is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels (WCAG 2.5.8).
accessibility.focusRingVisible: Ring on keyboard focus only, 3:1 against the adjacent colors.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: A console warning when label is empty.

keyboard.Tab: Moves focus to and from the switch; a disabled switch is skipped.
keyboard.Enter: Does not toggle; submits the owning form, as a native checkbox does.

aria: role=switch on the inner input; its checked state is exposed as aria-checked by the native input.
aria-describedby points to the description and, while validation is error, the error message.
required is exposed through the native required attribute.
announcements: Name, role switch and on or off on focus; the new state on toggle.

useCases.when: A setting turns on or off and applies as soon as it is flipped.
useCases.use: Switch with label, name and value.

useCases.when: A setting needs a hint or a reason it is unavailable.
A required acknowledgement is missing on submit.
useCases.use: Switch with required, validation error and errorMessage.

antiPatterns.pattern: A switch whose change only takes effect after the form is submitted.
antiPatterns.why: A switch signals an immediate effect; a deferred one reads as a bug.
The control has no accessible name; the component warns in the console.

antiPatterns.pattern: Choosing one of several options with switches.
antiPatterns.why: Switches are independent; they do not exclude each other.

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG)?
openQuestions.recommendation: Draft from the API vocabulary, and the WAI-ARIA APG switch pattern.
openQuestions.answer: Done in this pass: names from spec/api.json, keyboard and role from the APG switch pattern, tokens alias existing semantic tokens. A screen-reader pass is part of the review before beta.

openQuestions.question: Is the on/off prop named selected or checked?
openQuestions.recommendation: selected, the registered name; checked is a registered alias to selected.
openQuestions.answer: selected. The inner input's checked property is set from it.

openQuestions.question: Does validation follow the native required check by itself?
openQuestions.recommendation: No: validation is author-set, like the other form controls, so the error look appears only when the author decides (usually after a submit attempt).
openQuestions.answer: Author-set. The native validity (:invalid, reportValidity) still works independently.

openQuestions.question: Which sizes?
openQuestions.recommendation: small and medium, from the registered size vocabulary, medium the default.

openQuestions.question: What does required mean for a switch?
openQuestions.recommendation: Same as a required native checkbox: valueMissing while off. Useful for an acknowledgement; document it, not forbid it.
openQuestions.answer: Invalid while off, valid while on.

openQuestions.question: Is the error message announced live when it appears?
openQuestions.recommendation: No live region: link it with aria-describedby and aria-invalid; focus on the control reads it. Avoids double announcements with reportValidity.
openQuestions.answer: describedby only. Revisit if the manual screen-reader pass finds it is missed.

openQuestions.question: Is a separate small track height needed?
openQuestions.recommendation: Reuse the existing size.control.sm for both until the size foundations offer a smaller step; the size difference is carried by track-height-small and track-height-medium so it can diverge without a contract change.
openQuestions.answer: PROPOSAL values; the builder confirms visual sizes against Storybook and adjusts the two tokens.
